Comments (English): [ Bosch 800 Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || We bought this dishwasher to replace our old top-of-the line Jenn Air dishwasher. This one looks sleek and is a nice addition to our home. The inside racks don't seem as solid as the Jenn Air. They seem a bit more rickety. But they seem to work fine as well. It also isn't as quiet as the Jenn Air (which was almost silent), but it is still pretty quiet. However, I will say from what I see, this dishwasher cleans far better than the Jenn Air. You have to be sure the cups and glasses are secured or the jets will knock them over. So, from a standpoint of what I want out of a dishwasher, this does the trick! Plus, the tilt adjustment on the upper rack is pretty cook as well in order to get odd-sized items onto the upper rack. The drying technology also seems to be working well. Nothing dries plastics that well, but this does okay all around. So far I would highly recommend this one.

It comes to mind. After being so stressed and hearing the same thing from the sales representative every time, I finally got a call saying they would install it. It was installed on February 23rd. But the counselor didn't sound sorry. The consumer who purchased the product felt like a criminal, as if he had made a mistake by asking for installation, and had scolded the customer service representative for no reason. My stress was so high during the 12 days that I couldn't get the installation done. This was the first time I felt this difficult and stressed while purchasing something.

Comments (English): [ GE Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || This machine is quiet and appearance aesthetically pleasing. What I don't like about it is the rack design. These two camps were always arguing. Those who had used it said, "It's a must-have. It's a life-changing item." Those who refused to believe it would always say, "It's just a waste of energy and water." I used to be a neutral person, leaning toward "it's not necessary," but this opportunity has completely shifted my mind. Comments (English): [ Quiet. Appears to clean well. Horrible design. ] || ---------------- || I like the quietness of the operation. So far it seems to clean well, which is the entire purpose. However. Whomever designed this machine did a horrible job. First--The control panel and lights are not visible when the door is closed, so seeing time left or the indicator lights is impossible unless the door is opened, and then the indicator lights turn-off! This is a 100% design fail. Second--While the "open door to pause" feature is a neat idea, the door is easily bumped open thereby causing operation to pause. A locking mechanism should have been included. Again, a product design fail. Third-- The simplistic nature of the control panel is somewhat intuitive, hower the instructions in the manual which should provide more information provide less than the necessary information. All types of extraneous info for the engineer, but not so much for the operator. Apparently this was written for and by the engineers and not control checked by first time users to see if the instructions to do certain things were clear. it requires prior knowledge of the product, or similar products. Lastly-- This is more of a personal gripe, but the loading trays, especially the utensil holder are also poorly designed. They tray provide a lot of "options" but fail to maximizr the space for the most commonly used dishes. Failure of optimization in an attempt to be more versatile. The utensil holder is flimsy and made of cheap plastic. This will likely break within a year, especially the "lifting portion". Unless these design flaws are changed in future designs, I would NOT recommend this product. I would also suggest the GE design team re-evaluate their design protocols and more imprtantly testing of the design and product manual.

Again, a product design fail.Third-- The simplistic nature of the control panel is somewhat intuitive, hower the instructions in the manual which should provide more information provide less than the necessary information. All types of extraneous info for the engineer, but not so much for the operator. They tray provide a lot of 'options' but fail to maximizr the space for the most commonly used dishes. Failure  of optimization in an attempt to be more versatile. The utensil holder is flimsy and made of cheap plastic. This will likely break within a year, especially the 'lifting portion'. Unless these design flaws are changed in future designs, I would NOT recommend this product.I would also suggest the GE design team re-evaluate their design protocols and more imprtantly testing of the design and product manual.

Comments (English): [ The Quietest Dishwasher I have ever owned! ] || ---------------- || (This review was collected as part of a promotion.) The machine is very quiet which is wonderful, but I think I will have a problem when I have family dinner. I have not yet figured out how to get my dishes, bowls, cups, glasses, etc., in the machine without overcrowding. The side that has the separater for stem glasses is a very snug fit for regular tumblers, the other side is almost useless if I have bowls in the next space. The cutlery holders have the divisions for individual items, but when the entire family (12 of us) is here for dinner, I would love remove or lift those dividers. But I have to admit, my dishes, etc., come out sparkling and the cycle, (Auto) is very quick. The slightly narrowness does make a difference from the USA makes. Doesn't seem a lot, but it does!

Sentence (English): I like the quietness of the operation.
Comments (English): [ Quiet. Appears to clean well. Horrible design. ] || ---------------- || I like the quietness of the operation. So far it seems to clean well, which is the entire purpose.However. Whomever designed this machine did a horrible job. First--The control panel and lights are not visible when the door is closed, so seeing time left or the indicator lights is impossible unless the door is opened, and then the indicator lights turn-off! This is a 100% design fail.Second--While the "open door to pause" feature is a neat idea, the door is easily bumped open thereby causing operation to pause. A locking mechanism should have been included. Again, a product design fail.Third-- The simplistic nature of the control panel is somewhat intuitive, hower the instructions in the manual which should provide more information provide less than the necessary information. All types of extraneous info for the engineer, but not so much for the operator. Apparently this was written for and by the engineers and not control checked by first time users to see if the instructions to do certain things were clear. it requires prior knowledge of the product, or similar products. Lastly-- This is more of a personal gripe, but the loading trays, especially the utensil holder are also poorly designed. They tray provide a lot of "options" but fail to maximizr the space for the most commonly used dishes. Failure of optimization in an attempt to be more versatile. The utensil holder is flimsy and made of cheap plastic. This will likely break within a year, especially the "lifting portion". Unless these design flaws are changed in future designs, I would NOT recommend this product.I would also suggest the GE design team re-evaluate their design protocols and more imprtantly testing of the design and product manual.

Comments (English): [ Upgraded Model Not So Great ] || ---------------- || I have been a Bosch dishwasher owner for years. I just purchased a new 300 series dishwasher for my new home. There are two "upgrades" that are not improvements, in my opinion. First, the top rack has been redesigned and is now without a row of prongs on the right side that allows full use of the two right rows. If you have stemwear to wash, the first row (under the flip-down grey shelves) is practically unusable. Second, there is no longer a light on the panel to tell you that the dishes are "clean". This may be a power-saving improvement, but the lack of the indicator light makes it difficult to tell of someone else in my household remembered to turn the dishwasher on. And, I do not want to have to check an app to tell if the dishes are clean. Bosch service has reviewed this issue and determined the indicator light has been removed from this model. The new model is still very quiet and cleans the dishes very well. If this was my first Bosch dishwasher purchase, I may not be as disappointed as I am.

Sentence (English): I did a lot of homework before buying a dishwasher.
Comments (English): I did a lot of homework before buying a dishwasher. After comparing the dishwashers of various mainstream brands, I finally chose Haier’s W5000S. First of all, because the color matches the cabinet very well, and the installation height is 765mm. Compared with the top of other brands of cabinets It can be put in normally without modification. 50000Pa and double-sided washing ensure the cleaning ability of the dishwasher. The control panel on the top is fully functional, unlike some models that only have part of the control program, and other functions require a mobile phone to use. After using it for a few days, I am basically satisfied. In addition, the customer service will answer all questions and can help solve problems in a timely manner. It taught me how to adjust the upper bowl basket to avoid collisions between the upper spray arm and the chopsticks. Finally, there is one thing to complain about. The machine is not equipped with a tee. The kitchen reformer uses something like glue to seal the drainage, which seriously affects the appearance. I hope Haier can add a tee in the future.
Comments (Original): 在买洗碗机之前做了好多功课，对比了各个主流品牌型号的洗碗机，最后还是选择了海尔的W5000S.首先是因为颜色与橱柜很搭，然后安装高度是765mm，对比其他品牌橱柜顶部不需要改造就可以正常的放入。50000Pa和双面洗保证了洗碗机的清洁能力。顶部的控制面板功能很全，不像有些机型只有部分控制程序，其他功能要手机才能使用。使用几天下来，基本满意。另外客服有问必答，能帮忙及时解决问题，教会了我怎样调好上碗篮，避免上喷臂和筷子发生碰撞。最后有一点需要吐槽，机器没有配三通，厨改师傅用类似胶水的东西做的密封排水，严重影响美观，我希望海尔以后能把三通也加上。

Sentence (English): I've had this microwave a year now.
Comments (English): [ Problems from the Start ] || ---------------- || I've had this microwave a year now. Right from the start, I had an issue where I would put the cook time in, and push 'start' and nothing would happen except the timer would count down. (See attached video, I hope it attaches) It took numerous re-trys to actually get the microwave to run. Right away I called the vendor I purchased from and I was told to call LG and set up a service call. I took a video of the problem too. I did the service call, I think it goes to India because the technician had a thick accent which was hard to understand. She basically told me to unplug, plug and 'reset'. This did not good, so an appointment was set up, but I was warned that if the microwave didn't indicate a fault when the service person was there, I would still have to pay for the service call. The Technician came to my home and of course, the microwave didn't act up while he was there. Basically he told me I was pushing the buttons too hard and not in the center of the button. Thankfully, he didn't charge me. It is now a year since I purchased this microwave and I continue to have the same problem but I have discovered the problem. When shutting the microwave door, it is necessary to lift up the door as you shut it. Obviously there is a contact not being made correctly in the latch mechanism. As long as I do this, the microwave starts every time. You know, I shouldn't have to do this! This is a poorly made product and I have a feeling LG knows this. I'm so unhappy! The warranty period is over, but it doesn't matter. I plan to rip this thing out and deliver back to the vendor who doesn't back up their products. Sorry LG, this experience has soured me on buying any more products from your line. It's your loss, I'm a retiree with a lot of money to spend and I'm updating my whole house!

Sentence (English): We purchased the KitchenAid KDFE204KPS from BestBuy to replace a Kenmore that stopped working.
Comments (English): [ Soooo quiet and cleans well! ] || ---------------- || We purchased the KitchenAid KDFE204KPS from BestBuy to replace a Kenmore that stopped working. The primary things I was looking for: 1) a very quiet dishwasher, 2) no handle that stuck out, and 3) clean notification. We were originally looking at Bosch's, but were told they require hard-wiring and we didn't know what our 1979 house had (turns out it had hard-wiring, so we got an outlet installed under the sink). I went to a Facebook group "HGTV Fixer Upper Show Followers" and searched for posts on dishwasher recommendations. Many followers commented on how much they loved their KitchenAid dishwashers, so we chose this brand in lieu of Bosch. We have had this dishwasher for about 6 weeks now. The good: So far, it cleans well, and it is SO QUIET! The normal wash cycle is also fairly quick. It has a 4-hour delay wash cycle option that I use if I start a wash before going to bed and the cycle is done when we wake up. There is a light on the control panel notifying the dishes are Clean. The (1st world problems) bad: The first few washes had a strange smell, but I think that was just because it was new and needed to get broken in a little. It no longer smells. The only thing I don't really like is the design of the upper rack (technically middle rack). The center row is elevated to give clearance to the spray arm below. I feel like things don't always sit properly in the middle rack due to its design, but I'm getting used to it. Overall, I am happy with this dishwasher.

The only thing that has taken a little bit of getting used to is the top rack configuration. Many of our taller glasses need to be leaned over vs being able to stack them straight up on our previous dishwasher. That being said, the 3rd top rack is very nice for washing larger kitchen utensils.

Overall a very impressive dishwasher.

Comments (English): [ Buzzing! ] || ---------------- || We purchased this dishwasher and had it installed by Lowes less than a week ago. It turns out that, while running, it emits a sound that is pretty much identical to what you get when a fluorescent lightbulb goes bad, and it lasts for the entire wash cycle. I checked KitchenAid's website and found a video that supposedly depicts normal noise from a new dishwasher, and that noise was only audible during the initial fill cycle. Again, our dishwasher makes that buzzing, humming noise for the entire wash cycle. Maybe I'm just noise sensitive, but I can't stand to be around that for 2 hours! I called KitchenAid for assistance, and they sent a repairman to inspect the dishwasher. The repairman isolated the noise to the wash pump, and told us that everything is functioning properly - that this is the noise we ought to expect. Had I known that, I would never have purchased this dishwasher! Now I'm going to have to see if there is any sound deadening material that will block that noise from the rest of the house. I hate that I just spent this much money on something that is so miserable to be around. DO NOT BUY this dishwasher if you are trying to find something quiet for your home. That buzz cuts through everything!

Sentence (English): Loved this dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Started smoking within 2 years! ] || ---------------- || Loved this dishwasher. Family of 6 and it worked great for the 2 years we had it. Always cleaned out the screens at the bottom and never had any serious issues regarding cleaning or smells (seriously, it cleaned great). Dishes came out CLEAN (plastic doesn't dry, but it never does with the newer dishwashers). Door latch sometimes would pop open but it was usually because the powder was over the line or there was powder in the latch. Never had a latch issue with gel dishwashing solution. However, last week (and THANK GOD I WAS HOME! ) I started smelling something burning while running a load of dishes. Thinking it was one of my kids going hard with a grilled cheese or leaving the stove on (which they never do, but I believe in possibilities) I came out into the kitchen to find smoke and what smelled like an electrical fire getting ready to start. Smoke was coming out of the hole where the power cord comes out of the dishwasher. My kitchen and living room was filling with smoke. My mother recently passed away, so we have a ramp on the back of the house. We quickly unplugged the dishwasher mid cycle and got it outside, down the ramp. The plug was SO HOT idk how it didn't catch my outlet on fire. This thing was around seven hundred and we only got 2 years out of it. I can't keep "renting" dishwashers at this price. I wish this worked out for me but the fact it nearly caught my house on fire now makes me never even want a built in one (this dishwasher in the built in was my go-to whenever we decide to do a kitchen remodel). After it cooled down and stopped smoking, we had to get the water out somehow to bring it to the recycling place (warranty is 1 year, we had this 2 years). We brought it back inside, plugged it in and ran it for 30 seconds to drain the water. No smoke in those 30 seconds but the electrical burning smell and heat was back so it was only a matter of time before it burnt up. Now I'm back to square one. May the odds be ever in your favor.

Always cleaned out the screens at the bottom and never had any serious issues regarding cleaning or smells (seriously, it cleaned great). Dishes came out CLEAN (plastic doesn't dry, but it never does with the newer dishwashers). Door latch sometimes would pop open but it was usually because the powder was over the line or there was powder in the latch. Never had a latch issue with gel dishwashing solution. However, last week (and THANK GOD I WAS HOME! ) I started smelling something burning while running a load of dishes. Thinking it was one of my kids going hard with a grilled cheese or leaving the stove on (which they never do, but I believe in possibilities) I came out into the kitchen to find smoke and what smelled like an electrical fire getting ready to start. Smoke was coming out of the hole where the power cord comes out of the dishwasher. My kitchen and living room was filling with smoke. My mother recently passed away, so we have a ramp on the back of the house. We quickly unplugged the dishwasher mid cycle and got it outside, down the ramp. The plug was SO HOT idk how it didn't catch my outlet on fire. This thing was around seven hundred and we only got 2 years out of it. I can't keep "renting" dishwashers at this price. I wish this worked out for me but the fact it nearly caught my house on fire now makes me never even want a built in one (this dishwasher in the built in was my go-to whenever we decide to do a kitchen remodel). After it cooled down and stopped smoking, we had to get the water out somehow to bring it to the recycling place (warranty is 1 year, we had this 2 years). We brought it back inside, plugged it in and ran it for 30 seconds to drain the water. No smoke in those 30 seconds but the electrical burning smell and heat was back so it was only a matter of time before it burnt up. Now I'm back to square one. May the odds be ever in your favor.

Anyway, this was my first time using a dishwasher, and I'm very satisfied with the price, the interior space, and the cleaning power. I highly recommend this dishwasher to anyone looking for a cost-effective dishwasher, especially for single-person households.

But part of learning the set up of the dishes and pots for a new dishwasher.

Comments (English): [ Nice upgrade ] || ---------------- || I had a premium Kitchen Aid dishwasher that did work well but decided to break down after about 4 years of use. I decided to try Bosch based on its reputation for quality. So far the performance of the dishwasher has been stellar. I love the crystal dry as most everything comes out dry except some random plastic containers that have a lip that holds water. The machine is very quite. Took a little while to adjust how to load plates, etc. as it is different from other dishwashers I have used. Two things I would change: The silverware baskets are very cheaply made and are a pain to use. I ordered stronger replacement baskets from the Bosch website and they are worlds better. They should just include them with the machine with purchase. The second thing that would be nice is with the "Speed 60" wash it would be nice to be able to enable crystal dry as well. It's not a big deal but it would be a great option. As far as reliability, we will see. I hope it lasts longer than my previous Kitchen Aid.

Comments (English): Dishwashers can be cleaned very well, there is no doubt about it. It is also very convenient to wash up and down. The single disinfection function on the panel is not just hot air drying, and the hot water is passed through one or two times before drying. The process takes 1.5 hours and consumes 4.5 liters of water, which is too long. If the elderly cook in my family, I often pick up one or two to dry first, and wash a few at a time... If the machine needs to be dried by hand washing, you can only choose antibacterial storage on the app, which can be ventilated and dried. It's just that you can only choose on the app, which is too troublesome.
